method: Uniform triangle-surface covariance followed by symmetric eigendecomposition, rather than equally weighted mesh vertices. CGAL documents triangle-area weighting and continuous-object PCA; implementation here is NumPy, not CGAL.
derivation: For uniform triangle barycentric coordinates, E[li]=1/3, E[li^2]=1/6, E[li*lj]=1/12. For centered vertices vi and s=sum vi, E[xx^T]=(sum vi vi^T+s s^T)/12. Weight each triangle by its area and sum. Center coordinates before forming moments.
scope: All four named visual layers of each ABXY button in the existing width-scaled candidate. Every mesh SHA256 is checked against the inventory.
harness: tests/test_button_surface_axes.py: analytic rectangle covariance, subdivision invariance, rigid transform covariance, degenerate/nonfinite rejection; 3 tests passed in existing GPU environment
observations: Outer Button and Interior minimum-variance directions differ by approximately 1.34 to 3.81 degrees across ABXY; Interior2 differs by 0.18 to 1.15 degrees.
Letter meshes differ from their outer Button direction by approximately 5.84 to 27.61 degrees, showing why a decorative letter is not a reliable source of button axis.
Minimum-variance direction is an unsigned geometric thin-direction estimate. It is not proof of a prismatic joint, press sign, travel, clearance or alignment to real 1708 guides.
decision: Retain geometry directions for future registration and inspection; do not promote them to target mechanical axes. No adoption threshold invented.
limitations: Uniform surface area is geometric weighting, not a physical density or mass distribution.
Repeated or nearly repeated eigenvalues can make principal directions ambiguous; all eigenvalues are retained rather than hiding conditioning.
Surface centroids are not physical centers of mass. Candidate scale is width-matched, not a verified 1708 dimension model.
